title: Ebagu Crafts Workshop in Busan: A Small Museum With Big Views Near the 168 Stairs
html:
If you've ever looked up photos of Busan, you've probably seen the colorful 168 Stairs climbing up a hillside neighborhood near Busan Station. What a lot of visitors miss is a small, free museum just a short walk from those stairs that tells you the story behind all those houses on the hill: the Ebagu Crafts Workshop (이바구공작소, Ibagu Gongjakso). "Ibagu" is old Busan dialect for "story," so the name roughly means "Story Workshop" — and it's a great first stop if you want to understand what you're looking at before you climb the hill.

What Is Ebagu Crafts Workshop?

This two-story building opened in 2013 as part of a project to revive the Sanbok-ro (산복도로) hillside area — "sanbok-ro" just means "mountainside road," which is exactly what this whole neighborhood is built on. After the Korean War (1950–1953), refugees with nowhere else to go settled on this steep slope above Busan's port, and their descendants still live here today. Ebagu Crafts Workshop works like a small community archive: it collects old photos, tools, and personal stories from people who grew up on this hill, and turns them into exhibits so visitors can understand what daily life here used to look like.

The displays change roughly every two months, so what you see can vary, but a fun constant is on the first floor: a corner where you can try on a retro Korean school uniform (교복, gyobok) from decades past and take photos — a favorite with visitors who want a souvenir picture that's a little different from the usual. Head up to the second floor and you'll find a large window and viewing deck looking straight out over the rooftops of Sanbok-ro toward Busan's port — one of the best quiet, uncrowded photo spots in the whole area, and a nice break if you've just climbed a hill to get here.

Good to Know Before You Go

  • Address: 14-13 Mangyang-ro 486beon-gil, Dong-gu, Busan (초량동, Choryang-dong)
  • Hours: 10:00–19:00 (9:00–18:00 on Sundays and public holidays)
  • Closed: Every Monday
  • Admission: Free
  • Phone: +82-51-468-0289 (Korean only — for English help, call the 1330 Korea Travel Hotline at +82-2-1330)

There's no elevator or wheelchair ramp mentioned for the building itself, and remember that the surrounding neighborhood is all steep hills and stairs, so this stop is easier for travelers who can manage some walking uphill.

Getting There

Ebagu Crafts Workshop sits on the same hillside as the 168 Stairs, about a 10–15 minute uphill walk from Busan Station (Busan Subway Line 1) — follow the signs for "Ibagu-gil" or "이바구길." If you're already visiting the 168 Stairs and the free inclined elevator next to them, this museum is an easy add-on: it sits just off the main Ibagu-gil walking route, so you can pop in before or after you tackle the stairs. Typing 35.1171267121, 129.0338450468 into Google Maps or Naver Map will take you straight to the door.

Since it's free and right along a route you might already be walking, it's worth the short detour even if you only have 15–20 minutes to spare — just double-check it's open if you're visiting on a Monday.

meta_description: A beginner's guide to Ebagu Crafts Workshop in Busan: a free hillside museum near the 168 Stairs with retro uniform photos and port views.
